title: How Brands Use AI Character Replace to Localize Video Ads (Without Reshooting)
summary: Replace your ad spokesperson for each market using AI, no reshoot needed. Full workflow using Magic Hour's Character Replace and Lip Sync tools.
body_markdown:
## **Quick Answer**


Brands are using AI character replacement to turn one spokesperson-led ad into multiple market versions without booking new talent or repeating the shoot. The workflow replaces the original spokesperson with a local face, then uses AI lip sync to match a dubbed audio track to the new performance.


## **TL;DR**


- **One shoot, multiple markets:** Create one hero commercial and adapt the spokesperson for each target market instead of producing separate shoots.
- **Step 1:** Use[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) to replace the original spokesperson while preserving the performance.
- **Step 2:** Use[Magic Hour Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) to synchronize the replacement spokesperson with localized audio.
- **What it replaces:** Repeated reshoots, talent rebooking, and separate production budgets for every market.


## **Intro**


A brand shoots one ad, but running it across five markets traditionally means five separate shoots. Companies that localize content can see **significantly higher conversion rates** than those that do not, making efficient localization a significant part of the growth strategy. This article explains the specific AI character replacement workflow brands are using to turn one shoot into localized video ads without reshooting for every market.


## **The Problem With Traditional Ad Localization**


A brand can shoot one strong commercial, but running it across five markets traditionally means rebooking talent, arranging travel, securing studio time, hiring production crews, and completing post-production for every version. Five markets can quickly turn into five separate shoots, with each version costing tens of thousands of dollars and taking weeks to complete.


That timeline also creates a media problem: by the time every localized version is ready, part of the campaign window may already be gone. AI character replacement offers a different model by keeping the original shoot and adapting the on-screen talent after production.


## **What AI Character Replacement Actually Does in an Ad Context**


Marketers often group character replacement, dubbing, and AI avatars together, but they solve different problems.


### **Character Replace vs Dubbing vs AI Avatars**


**Approach**


**What It Does**


**Best For**


**AI Dubbing / Lip Sync only**


Keeps the original spokesperson and syncs new audio to their mouth movements


When the original talent is appropriate for all markets


**AI Avatar**


Generates a virtual presenter from scratch


When no original footage exists


**AI Character Replace**


Swaps the original spokesperson with a local face while keeping the original performance


When you want a local face in existing footage without reshooting


Character replacement becomes more valuable when the original spokesperson is not culturally appropriate or recognizable in the target market. Dubbing can change the language, but it cannot change who the audience sees on screen.


## **The Workflow: One Shoot, Multiple Market Versions**


### **1. Shoot Once With Any On-Camera Talent**


The hero production can remain straightforward: one spokesperson, one set, one production day, and one finished commercial. That source footage becomes the foundation for every regional version, so its lighting, framing, camera movement, and performance quality set the ceiling for the final outputs.


### **2. Replace the Spokesperson for Each Market**


With[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , the team uploads the source video and a reference photo of the local spokesperson or talent. The AI preserves the original performance, timing, camera movement, and background while replacing the primary character; the workflow described in the earlier[actor replacement guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-replace-an-actor-in-a-video-without-reshooting) covers the underlying process in more detail.


Each generation currently supports clips up to **15 seconds** , which fits many short-form advertising formats. Commercial use requires a paid plan.


### **3. Sync Localized Audio**


The next layer is language. Upload the character-replaced video to[Magic Hour Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) along with the dubbed audio for the target market, and the tool synchronizes the replacement spokesperson's mouth movements to the new track.


This separates the visual localization problem from the language problem: Character Replace changes who appears on screen, while Lip Sync adapts how that person speaks. A dedicated[AI lip sync guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-lip-sync-a-video-with-ai) can cover the audio workflow in more detail.


### **4. Review and Export**


The final review should check character consistency across frames, lip sync accuracy, and whether the original background and scene still look natural. Paid Character Replace outputs remove watermarks and include commercial use rights, making the result suitable for a production workflow.


## **Where This Works Best (And Where It Has Limits)**


### **Where It Works Best**


- **Spokesperson-led product demos** where the talent is clearly visible and the background remains consistent.
- **Short-form ads under 15 seconds** where the current Character Replace generation limit aligns with the format.
- **Markets where a recognizable local face matters** more than the original spokesperson's fame.
- **A/B testing different spokesperson looks** in the same ad before committing additional production budget.


### **Current Limitations to Know Before You Pitch This Internally**


- The current **15-second generation limit** covers many social ad formats but not longer brand films or TV spots.
- Footage with **fast movement, heavy occlusion, or multiple interacting subjects** can produce less stable results.
- The **reference photo quality matters directly** : a sharp, well-lit professional image generally produces better results than a casual snapshot.
- **Commercial use requires a paid Magic Hour plan** , so the workflow is best suited to teams with an allocated production budget.


## **Real Use Cases Marketers Are Running With This**


- Replace a US-based spokesperson with a local presenter for a regional launch without rebooking talent or studio time.
- Test two different spokesperson looks in the same 10-second ad before committing production budget to either.
- Update a training or onboarding video after a spokesperson leaves the company without recreating the original recording.
- Create market-specific product demos where the presenter matches the demographic of each target audience.
- Build a campaign concept deck showing different talent directions in the same footage before a client approves casting.


## **Cost and Time Comparison**


### **Traditional multi-market production:**


- Separate shoot per market: days of production for each version
- Talent rebooking, travel, and studio fees per market
- Post-production for every version
- Timeline: weeks per market version


### **AI character replacement workflow:**


- One hero shoot
- Character Replace per market: minutes per version
- Lip Sync per market: minutes per version
- Timeline: hours per market version once the hero shoot exists


AI video production can significantly reduce advertising production costs compared with traditional shoots, although the savings vary by production scale, creative requirements, and number of markets.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Is AI character replacement legal for commercial ads?**


Magic Hour's paid plans permit commercial use of generated outputs. You also need the appropriate rights or model release for any real person used as the replacement reference; using someone's likeness without consent is not made permissible simply because AI generated the video.


### **How realistic does the replacement look in a professional ad?**


The strongest results come from clear, well-lit footage paired with a professional reference photo. Fast movement, heavy occlusion, and complex interactions can make the replacement less stable, so generating **3 to 5 variations** and selecting the most consistent result is a practical quality-control approach.


### **What ad formats and lengths does this support?**


The current **15-second Character Replace limit** covers many TikTok, Reels, YouTube Shorts, and Meta feed placements. Longer brand films or TV spots exceed the current generation limit, so teams working with longer creative need to divide the project into shorter scenes.


### **How long does the AI character replacement process take per market version?**


Character Replace typically takes **30 seconds to just over one minute** per clip, depending on length and complexity. Lip Sync adds a similar processing window, meaning five 15-second market versions can be generated in under an hour of processing time rather than weeks of production.


### **Does the background change when you replace the spokesperson?**


In **Character Mode** , the original background, scene, and camera work are preserved while the primary subject changes. **Scene Mode** regenerates the character and background, which is useful when a market version needs a different environment as well as a different spokesperson.
